title: Groundnut Soup, Cameroon Style
author: Omolabake for #OunjeAladun
desc: Boiled, blended raw groundnuts and garlic simmered in a fried pepper base with beef stock, crayfish, assorted meats and smoked fish, finished with sliced ugu leaves.
longDesc: The page’s title is ‘Groundnut Soup Cameroon Style’; the author says it is popular in parts of Cameroon, Togo and Benin. Raw groundnuts are soaked, peeled, boiled about 10 minutes (the page warns not to skip this or the soup tastes raw) and blended with garlic. Diced onion is fried, blitzed peppers cooked about 7 minutes on low-medium heat, then the groundnut paste, stock, crayfish, salt and seasoning cubes added with the lid on for about 10 minutes. Meats and smoked fish go in until the water reduces down, and the ugu leaves simmer 3 minutes before the heat goes off.
ingredients: 200 g sliced ugu leaves (about two small bunches)
Cooked assorted meats and smoked fish — quantity not printed
2 cooked rich beef stock (printed with no unit)
steps: Soak the groundnuts and peel off the skins. (The soaking time is not printed.)
Boil the groundnuts about 10 minutes — the page says not to skip this or the soup will taste of raw groundnut. Blend with the garlic.
Fry the onions in the oil. Add the blitzed peppers and cook about 7 minutes on low-medium heat.
Add the groundnut paste, stock, crayfish, salt and seasoning cubes. Put the lid on for about 10 minutes.
Add the meats and smoked fish and cook until the water reduces down.
Add the sliced ugu leaves, simmer 3 minutes and turn off the heat.
chefTips: The printed cue for the meats stage is ‘till the water reduces down’.
Boil the groundnuts first; the page is firm about this.
‘2 cooked rich beef stock’ is printed with no unit — use enough to loosen the paste and note the gap.
commonMistakes: Boiling the ugu leaves too long.
Guessing the stock amount without watching the soup’s thickness.
healthBenefits: Groundnuts, meat and fish add protein; ugu leaves add greens.
culturalNote: The page title attributes the style to Cameroon and says the soup is popular in parts of Cameroon, Togo and Benin, noting a link to Calabar. The attribution is the author’s own, and Cameroon is the only country the title names.
sources: Title as printed: ‘Groundnut Soup Cameroon Style’. Byline as printed: ‘Omolabake for #OunjeAladun’ (flagged: first name plus site tag). ‘June 30, 2020’. Yield and total time not printed (servings 6 and the prep/cook split are placeholders for the app). TWO-PASS.
